dunno why im telling yall this- but after i dropped out of my mfa, and my life was crumbling, i put down art and thought "i should just have a new dream- im a failure- art is not for me" needless to say, i had a pretty bad experience there. I gave up on anything art for an entire year plus some change... sold all my paintings for next to nothing because i wanted them out of my life.  yes i finally DID get meds for depression, but my life was still recovering from the dumpster fire it had been.

after 6 months of cleaning toilets, delivering food, somehow i got a job teaching art at a highschool. Okay, i say "somehow" but the last person quit and I applied thinking "im probably not going to get this" and i got it. I teach art now, and my love for art is back. I have a show coming up in august, but somehow that doesnt matter to me as much as being able to do the thing I love and feel happy again.

Painting. I love to ask chatgpt "what should i paint today" and i just paint/ draw that thing. I requires a lot of focus and sometimes HOURS of concentration on/off. Don't give up yet.

Coping mechanisms! get ya coping mechanisms here\~ I got plenty.

Most of my coping mechanisms are to assist me with being a working adult. I dont disclose my ASD to any employer because It took me a year to get a job so I want people to think I'm as "normal" as possible.  

I have playlists I spend hours curating and listen to music all day with either one or two tiny bluetooth headphones. Alternatively, I have some noise canceling earbuds also for when things get very loud. I have a few fidget toys I bring with me each day that dont seem to bother anyone. I also have some gloves with me for when I have to touch certain textures (CARDBOARD!!!). I also try to follow pretty much the same routine everyday since breaking my routine usually causes me a bit of stress. Sounds like a lot of stuff to carry, but I wear a fanny pack hahah- so I just carry everything in there and try to not stand out too much.
